title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-17
body:
Context:
- Symptom: throughput dropped ~25-35% for long-tail workloads after 2026-01-28 release (model runtime change + batching tuning). Latency P95 largely OK, but overall RPS sustained lower under same client load. Observed during canary->prod ramp.
- Affected: hosted API + a subset of dedicated pools on G4/RTX nodes. Not all regions.
- Hypothesis (initial): continuous-batching misconfiguration (idle flush / max batch) or change in request size distribution causing smaller avg batch sizes. Also possible KV cache hit-rate regression increasing per-request compute and reducing batching opportunities.

Quick sanity metrics (promQL we ran):
- total RPS by pod: sum(rate(redwood_requests_total[1m])) by (pod)
- avg batch size: avg_over_time(batch_size_sum[5m]) / avg_over_time(batch_size_count[5m])  (proxy metric names: batcher_batch_size_sum, batcher_batch_size_count)
- kv cache hit rate: increase(kv_cache_hits[5m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests[5m])
- observed in canary: avg batch size dropped from ~54 -> ~12 over 24h window
- kv cache hit-rate dropped 83% -> 46% on affected pods

Commands / queries I ran (notes + outputs):
1) Pod logs (grep for batcher / flush messages)
- kubectl -n inference logs deploy/model-runtime-rt-1 -c runtime | egrep "batcher|idle_flush|max_batch" --line-buffered | tail -n 200
  -> repeated: "INFO batcher: flush due to idle_timeout (idle_flush=true) inflight=1 target_batch=64 actual_batch=1"
  -> lots of these at 10-50ms intervals which suggests tiny batches being flushed early.

2) Inspect runtime config in pod (mounted configmap):
- kubectl -n inference exec -it deploy/model-runtime-rt-1 -- cat /etc/runtime/config.yaml | sed -n '1,200p'
  runtime.continuous_batching.enabled: true
  runtime.continuous_batching.max_batch_size: 64
  runtime.continuous_batching.idle_flush_ms: 20  # <-- suspect this is too low after tokenization changes
  runtime.continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens: 4096

3) Prometheus comparison of batch size around deploy window:
- recorded: avg(batch_size) 2026-01-27: 54, 2026-01-29: 12
- query: avg_over_time(batcher_batch_size[1h])

4) Quick load test locally against canary (k6 script):
- k6 run --vus 400 --duration 5m load-tests/long-tail-seq.js --summary-export=out.json
  -> under same VUs, throughput ~18% less vs pre-deploy binary; 95th latency similar. Batch histograms show shift to more single-request flushes.

Error/log snippets saved:
- "WARN batcher: idle_flush triggered; inflight=2 target_batch=64 actual_batch=1 idle_flush_ms=20"
- "DEBUG kv-cache: miss key=xyz123, miss_count=1"
- "ERROR runtime: request execution slower than expected, seq_len=2048, exec_ms=1200"

What changed in the release?
- Model-runtime binary bumped (v2.14.0 -> v2.15.0) - PR included tokenization fix and minor network optimizations (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789).
- Config tweaks: we lowered idle_flush_ms from 50 -> 20 to reduce latency spikes for short sequences.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) idle_flush_ms now too small for new tokenization behavior: tokenization now emits tokens earlier/later causing request arrival pattern such that continuous-batcher sees sparse arrivals and flushes early -> smaller batches -> lower throughput.
2) KV cache regression: tokenization fix changed cache key formatting -> hit-rate drop, more first-token work, longer exec time -> less overlap to form batches.
3) Autoscaler behaviour / node churn causing pods to have lower aggregate arrival -> smaller batch sizes. Less likely because we see same pod-level pattern.
4) Networking: keepalive/tcp settings cause request bursts to be smaller. Lower probability.

Experiments run so far (results):
- Increase idle_flush_ms to 80ms on a canary subset (10% traffic) -> avg batch size recovered to ~38, throughput improved ~15% vs canary baseline, no significant P95 regression. (Configured via configmap rollout to runtime-config-canary)
- Force kv-cache diagnostic: dump keys on miss to check key formatting -> found a few patterns where prefix changed (tokenizer now normalizes punctuation) -> kv keys for some cached prefixes mismatched.
- Temporary rollback of runtime binary on one pool -> throughput returned to baseline for that pool. Strong indicator binary change + config tuning interplay.

Quick experiment plan (next steps):
- Short-term (0-24h):
  1) Roll out idle_flush_ms -> 80ms for affected pools (canary then rollout) as hotfix.
  2) Add targeted telemetry: per-request tokenization phase timing (metric: tokenization_ms), and per-batcher arrival inter-arrival histogram.
  3) Add a compatibility shim in cache key generation to accept both old/new prefixes for 48h to recover hit-rate.
- Medium-term (24h-2w):
  1) Reproduce locally with tokenization change + synthetic traffic to tune idle_flush_ms vs latency SLO.
  2) Add adaptive flush: flush threshold dynamically adjusts based on recent inter-arrival times / seq length distribution.
  3) Add a regression test: load-test harness that asserts avg batch size does not fall below X for a representative workload when changing tokenizer.

Commands to roll the quick hotfix (notes):
- kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config --patch '{"data":{"continuous_batching.idle_flush_ms":"80"}}' && kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/model-runtime-rt-1
- Monitor: grafana dashboard (batching overview) + alert: avg_batch_size_drop > 30% for 10m

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need to audit tokenizer change PR for any implicit cache-key or prefix changes; flag PR authors (Mateo) to confirm intent.
- Is there a reason idle_flush_ms was set to 20 in the release? Was there a perf regression on short seqs we are compensating for? (Check #runtime-perf-slack thread)
- Validate whether adaptive flush increases tail latency for very small sequences; measure P99 before/after.

Relevant links / artifacts:
- PR with tokenization change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789
- Infra incident ticket (created): JIRA-4821
- Temporary canary config: runtime-config-canary (k8s configmap)

Notes for post-mortem skeleton (if hotfix required):
- Timeline of deploy -> detection -> mitigation (hotfix) -> verification
- Root cause: tokenizer change -> cache-key drift + aggressive idle_flush_ms -> smaller batch sizes
- Contributing factors: lack of load/regression test for tokenizer changes, config defaults tuned for older arrival patterns
- Actions: add regression tests, adaptive batching, cache compatibility shim, improved pre-merge telemetry for tokenization changes

Personal to-do (tomorrow): check cache key dump results with Priya and push shim patch, coordinate hotfix rollout with SRE and CS (notice customers if any impact), update Runbook entry for batching tuning.

End of scratchpad.
